thread.title: Goldman Sachs targets Apple for credit card

author: Anthony Noto
title: Goldman Sachs targets Apple for credit card
text: – Reporter, New York Business Journal May 11, 2018, 6:45am HST For years, financial giant Goldman Sachs Group Inc. has advised Apple Inc . on a variety of ventures, including M&A deals and fundraising initiatives. Now, the relationship is taking a new turn. The two companies reportedly are looking to create a credit card, one that's sold at Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) retail stores. The pursuit marks the Wall Street firm’s first foray into plastic, according to The Wall Street Journal . The initiative would pit Goldman (NYSE: GS) against credit card companies like JPMorgan Chase & Co. (NYSE: JPM) and Citigroup Inc. (NYSE: C). It is not yet known which card network — Visa Inc., Mastercard Inc. or Discover Financial Services — would process transactions for a Goldman/Apple card. A launch date is slated for early 2019. The joint venture would require the Cupertino, California-based tech giant to replace its rewards-card partnership with Barclays PLC, which began issuing the Apple credit card in 2005. The move also seems to be a departure from the direction Apple had been headed, with a focus on mobile payments via the iPhone. Adoption of the so-called Apple Pay system has been slower than executives had hoped, according to the WSJ report. The move does, however, coincide with Goldman's ongoing attempt to attract middle-market customers after traditionally being a go-to adviser for high-net-worth individuals. Last year , Goldman expanded into local banking and started issuing online loans of a few thousand dollars. Individuals once needed $10 million to get the attention of Goldman’s elite private bankers. Today, under the brand Marcus — named after founder Marcus Goldman — customers can open a savings account with as little as $1. The credit card offering also is being seen as compensation of some sorts for what is believed to be a slump in securities trading . The partnership would extend into other services including Goldman offering in-store loans to Apple customers buying iPhones and other gadgets. – Reporter, New York Business Journal May 11, 2018, 6:45am HST Related Content
